question: What is the primary objective of control therapy in oncology?

options.A: Achieve complete eradication of malignant cells
options.B: Provide total symptom relief without extending life
options.C: Halt disease progression and manage tumor burden
options.D: Prevent the initial genetic mutation of cells

explanation: Control therapy focuses on keeping the cancer from spreading further and reducing the tumor size when a complete cure is not possible. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h1)

question: A patient with widespread, incurable metastasis is admitted for pain control and comfort measures. Which treatment goal is guiding this care plan?
explanation: Palliative care prioritizes comfort and quality of life when the disease can no longer be cured or controlled. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h1)

question: The primary purpose of a diagnostic surgical biopsy in oncology is to...

options.A: Completely eradicate the primary tumor site
options.B: Obtain tissue samples for histological confirmation
options.C: Remove organs at high genetic risk of malignancy
options.D: Relieve acute obstruction and severe hemorrhage

explanation: Diagnostic surgery directly samples tumor tissue so pathologists can confirm the exact cell type and cancer stage. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why would a surgeon perform a debulking procedure for a patient with an advanced, incurable tumor?

options.A: To relieve pressure on surrounding vital structures and reduce pain
options.B: To completely cure the patient by removing all microscopic traces
options.C: To stimulate the patient's immune system to attack remaining cells
options.D: To prevent the original tumor cells from mutating into a new cancer

explanation: Debulking is a palliative measure that lessens the physical burden of a large tumor mass to improve the patient's comfort. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which radiation therapy destroys cancer cells?

options.A: Stimulating the patient's white blood cells
options.B: Altering the systemic pH of the body
options.C: Damaging cellular DNA to cause cell death
options.D: Blocking the blood supply to the tumor bed

explanation: Ionizing radiation directly breaks down the genetic material within cells, halting their ability to divide and survive. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which instruction is essential for a nurse to provide to a patient receiving external beam radiation to the neck?

options.A: Apply a tight synthetic bandage to protect the skin from sunlight
options.B: Scrub the skin markings vigorously with an antiseptic sponge daily
options.C: Use heating pads frequently on the neck to relieve muscle stiffness
options.D: Avoid applying commercial lotions or perfumes to the marked treatment area

explanation: Substances like lotions can react with radiation or trap heat on the skin, worsening burns; skin markings must also be preserved and never scrubbed off. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary risk associated with the extravasation of a vesicant chemotherapy agent?

options.A: Severe local tissue necrosis and sloughing
options.B: Rapid elevation of systemic blood pressure
options.D: Permanent damage to the cardiac muscle

explanation: Vesicants are blistering agents that cause severe, destructive damage to subcutaneous tissues if they leak outside the vein. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h4)

question: A patient receiving outpatient chemotherapy calls the clinic reporting a temperature of 38.5°C. What is the most appropriate initial nursing instruction?

options.A: Drink plenty of cold fluids and recheck the temperature in six hours
options.B: Apply a cold compress to the forehead to bring the fever down safely
options.C: Report immediately to the emergency facility for a full sepsis workup
options.D: Take an extra dose of prescribed oral vitamins and rest at home

explanation: Fever in a neutropenic patient is an oncological emergency indicating potential sepsis, requiring immediate medical evaluation and broad-spectrum antibiotics. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h4)

question: How do targeted therapies differ fundamentally from traditional cytotoxic chemotherapy?

options.A: They focus on specific molecular pathways unique to cancer cells
options.B: They exclusively target normal rapidly dividing mucosal cells
options.C: They only work when administered directly into the spinal column
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for any supportive nursing care

explanation: Targeted agents are designed to interfere with specific molecules needed for tumor growth, rather than targeting all dividing cells indiscriminately. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the underlying cause of immune-related adverse events during immunotherapy?

options.A: Bacterial contamination of the intravenous medication bag
options.B: Enhanced immune activity attacking normal healthy organs
options.C: Direct toxic destruction of bone marrow stem cells
options.D: Severe allergic hypersensitivity to synthetic preservatives

explanation: By taking the brakes off the immune system, immunotherapy can prompt T-cells to attack healthy host tissues, causing inflammatory side effects. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which electrolyte imbalances are classic hallmarks of tumor lysis syndrome?
explanation: The massive lysis of cancer cells releases large amounts of intracellular potassium and phosphate directly into the circulation. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h6)

question: A patient with lung cancer develops facial swelling, engorged neck veins, and shortness of breath. Which oncological emergency is most likely occurring?
explanation: Obstruction or compression of the superior vena cava impairs venous return from the upper body, producing characteristic facial and neck edema. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of the World Health Organization analgesic ladder in cancer care?

options.A: To calculate the exact chemotherapy dose required for tumor regression
options.B: To guide a systematic, step-wise approach to pain management
options.C: To determine the safe timeline for radiation therapy fractionation
options.D: To measure the functional status and mobility of palliative patients

explanation: The WHO ladder helps clinicians select appropriate pain medications based on pain severity, escalating from non-opioids to strong opioids as needed. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why is it important to administer antiemetic medications proactively before a patient receives moderately emetogenic chemotherapy?

options.A: It prevents the direct physical rupture of gastrointestinal blood vessels
options.B: Proactive dosing eliminates the risk of developing total bone marrow failure
options.C: Antiemetics lose all chemical stability if taken after vomiting begins
options.D: It is significantly easier to prevent nausea than to stop it once it has started

explanation: Preventative antiemetic therapy blocks neurotransmitter pathways before they are triggered by chemotherapy agents, offering far superior control. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h7)

question: At what point in the disease trajectory should palliative care ideally be introduced for a patient with cancer?

options.A: Strictly when the patient is discharged home without nursing support
options.B: Only after all curative chemotherapy options have completely failed
options.C: Exclusively during the final twenty-four hours of active dying
options.D: Alongside disease-directed treatment early in the course of illness

explanation: Modern guidelines recommend integrating palliative care early to manage symptoms and distress concurrently with active cancer treatments. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h8)

question: Which nursing action best demonstrates effective psychosocial support for a newly diagnosed oncology patient?

options.A: Assuring the family that the patient will definitely be cured with modern therapy
options.B: Focusing exclusively on physical vital signs to prevent emotional overwhelm
options.C: Directing the patient to avoid discussing emotional worries to maintain optimism
options.D: Providing a safe space for the patient and family to express fears and ask questions

explanation: Open communication and validating emotional distress are core components of compassionate, holistic psychosocial nursing care. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h8)
